title: Wytham Woods (England) — deciduous forest, every tree as ground truth (Q-ForestLab)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ) from the Q-ForestLab instance segmentation benchmark (Ghent University). Test area of the Wytham Woods plot (temperate deciduous forest, Oxfordshire, England). Every point carries the manually assigned tree ID (122 reference trees ≥ 10 cm DBH). Canopy height (H95) 19 m, PAI proxy 3.6, cover 87 %; 12.1 % of the light reaches the ground vertically (estimate from the point cloud, no occlusion correction). Source: Zenodo 16875688, CC BY 4.0.

title: Ofental (Berchtesgaden National Park) — coniferous forest, every tree as ground truth (Q-ForestLab)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ) from the Q-ForestLab instance segmentation benchmark (Ghent University). Test area of the Ofental plot (dense, steep alpine coniferous forest; Ofental in Ramsau near Berchtesgaden, Berchtesgaden National Park; map pin = village of Ramsau, approximate). Every point carries the manually assigned tree ID (58 reference trees ≥ 10 cm DBH). Canopy height (H95) 16 m, PAI proxy 19.2, cover 96 %; 3.7 % of the light reaches the ground vertically (estimate from the point cloud, no occlusion correction). Source: Zenodo 16875688, CC BY 4.0.

title: Litchfield (Northern Territory) — tropical savanna, every tree as ground truth (Q-ForestLab)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ) from the Q-ForestLab instance segmentation benchmark (Ghent University). Test area of the Litchfield plot (tropical savanna, TERN SuperSite, Northern Territory, Australia). Every point carries the manually assigned tree ID (44 reference trees ≥ 10 cm DBH). Canopy height (H95) 17 m, PAI proxy 2.1, cover 41 %; 57.9 % of the light reaches the ground vertically (estimate from the point cloud, no occlusion correction). Source: Zenodo 16875688, CC BY 4.0.

title: Large old tree, Brazil — what the ground scanner misses in the crown (Q-ForestLab)
description: Large old tropical tree (Brazil) from the Q-ForestLab dataset on terrestrial and canopy laser scanning (D'hont, Calders et al.). Switch below: ground scan only vs. ground + canopy scan; the colouring 'Canopy scan only' shows in orange what the ground scanner misses (23 % of the wood points). In the cylinder model (TreeQSM, mean of 10 runs) the canopy scan adds +38 % branch length, +20 % branches and +5 % wood volume (20.7 → 21.8 m³). Source: Zenodo 15880857, CC BY 4.0.

title: Robson Creek (Queensland) — tropical rainforest, every tree as ground truth (Q-ForestLab)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ) from the Q-ForestLab instance segmentation benchmark (Ghent University). Test area (20 m × 25 m) of the Robson Creek plot, a TERN SuperSite in the tropical rainforest of Far North Queensland, Australia. Every point carries the manually assigned tree ID (52 reference trees ≥ 10 cm DBH). Measured against them, 3DFin finds 45 (86 %) at 84 % precision; the suite's own single-tree segmentation separates 25 % of the trees with IoU ≥ 0.5. Canopy height (H95) 20 m, PAI proxy 10.7, cover 98 %; 1.1 % of the light reaches the ground vertically (estimate from the point cloud, no occlusion correction). Source: Zenodo 16875688, CC BY 4.0.

title: Semperoper — twenty archive photos, back in place
description: Structure from motion from twenty historical photographs of the Deutsche Fotothek, none with a known camera position. Reconstructed are the point cloud of the building and the position of every photographer, including the estimated focal length. 20 of 20 photos located, median 6.8 % position and 2.1° direction deviation against the reference model, one misregistration. Dataset HistImage2021 (F. Maiwald, TU Dresden, CC BY-SA 4.0), photos SLUB Dresden / Deutsche Fotothek.

title: Eifel beech — terrestrial scan of a single tree (28 m)
description: Terrestrial point cloud from the beech stand in the Eifel (4.4 million points, 27.6 m tall), from the same study as the 360° image. DELIBERATELY WITHOUT INVENTORY MARKERS: at breast height the cloud carries a dense, non-circular mass (32,000 points over 1.8 m, circle-fit residual 29 cm), while the vertically continuous columns give only 11 cm diameter — impossible for a 27.6 m tree. The stem base is evidently poorly sampled, the crown dense. Without the authors' workflow (TreeLS, assignment of points to the target tree) no reliable DBH can be derived here; printing a number would be dishonest. The scene thus shows a limit of the chain: not every single-tree cloud supports an inventory.

title: Eifel beech stand — 360° image from a VR study
description: Near-ground 360° panorama of a beech stand in the Eifel, taken for the study 'Advancing Forest Monitoring and Assessment Through Immersive Virtual Reality' (Wageningen University & Research). Covers the chain's equirectangular input with a real forest panorama from a peer-reviewed study. The image carries NO camera pose and therefore runs through the pass-through branch, not the reprojection — unlike the scanner RGB images, whose pose comes with the E57.

title: Vienna Woods spruce-dominated mixed stand — TLS with semantic ground truth (SegmentedForests plot_07)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (Riegl VZ-400i) of a spruce-dominated mixed stand in the Vienna Woods, every point manually classified. The ground-truth counterpart to the Renon scene: same species, same acquisition type, but with known truth. 128 labelled reference stems. 3DFin finds 94.5 % of them at 100 % precision, the suite's numpy baseline only 34.4 % at 74.6 %. Source: SegmentedForests (MIT).

title: Vienna Woods beech — TLS with semantic ground truth (SegmentedForests plot_06)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (Riegl VZ-2000i) of a European beech stand in the Vienna Woods, every point MANUALLY classified: stem, branches + leaves, ground, shrub, lying deadwood, non-vegetation. The first scene of the suite with real truth at point level — detection and segmentation can be measured here, not just compared with each other. Baseline detection reaches 60 % recall at 42 % precision on this plot; with the stem continuity check 57 % / 71 %. Source: SegmentedForests (MIT).

title: SYSSIFOSS arboretum — 11 trees, 6 species
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ-400) of single trees from Central European mixed forest plots near Bretten and Karlsruhe. 11 trees (1× sycamore maple, 1× Douglas fir, 2× Norway spruce, 2× European beech, 2× red oak, 1× sessile oak, 2× Scots pine). SYNTHETIC arrangement on a 16 m grid: the original locations are spread over ~20 km. Geometry, height and diameter of every tree are unchanged — an arboretum for comparing species. Colouring = the dataset's manual leaf/wood separation (green = leaf/needle, brown = wood, ground truth); DBH is fitted from wood points only. No panorama in the dataset. Source: SYSSIFOSS, heiDATA doi:10.11588/DATA/UUMEDI, CC BY 4.0.

title: SYSSIFOSS plot BR01 — beech & sessile oak
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ-400) of single trees from Central European mixed forest plots near Bretten and Karlsruhe. 2 trees (1× European beech, 1× sessile oak). Plot BR01: the two trees stand in their REAL relative position (EPSG:25832), 50 m apart — the space between them is freely walkable. Colouring = the dataset's manual leaf/wood separation (green = leaf/needle, brown = wood, ground truth); DBH is fitted from wood points only. No panorama in the dataset. Source: SYSSIFOSS, heiDATA doi:10.11588/DATA/UUMEDI, CC BY 4.0.

title: Renon — 4 scan positions, full analysis (ITCD, DBH, QSM, projection)
description: Real RGB point cloud from four registered terrestrial scans (E57) at the Renon site (ICOS IT-Ren), 28.8 million raw points, with the complete analysis chain on top: 64 trees on 0.126 ha (509 stems/ha, 45.8 m²/ha basal area, median DBH 24 cm). Single-tree segmentation (ITCD) via shortest paths in the point graph, switchable against the RGB view; DBH by six methods with consensus and spread per tree; QSM cylinder model with stem taper; growth projection to 2056 from the real TreeGrOSS/BWINPro engine (NW-FVA, GPLv3). The stand is uneven-aged: age comes per tree from height via the model's site-index function (site index 10.5 m, derived from h100 = 22.1 m at 200 years for the upper layer), not from a single stand age. Without a field inventory, the DBH comparison shows agreement, not accuracy.

title: Renon setup 002 — RGB point cloud (walkable)
description: Real RGB point cloud of a terrestrial scan (E57) at the Renon site (ICOS IT-Ren), measured colour per point. 3,384,990 points after thinning, walkable. A second scan position next to renon-setup01 — the scan shadows fall differently, the stand becomes visible from another position. Source: E57 (6 pinhole cameras + point cloud), open Renon dataset.

title: Hedgerow Flanders — alders (site M)
description: Terrestrial laser scan (RIEGL VZ-1000) of trees from hedgerows and tree rows in the agricultural landscape of Flanders. 19 trees (19× alder) in their co-registered positions; colouring = true tree membership from the dataset (ground truth, no segmentation). No panorama in the dataset. Source: Zenodo 4487116, CC BY 4.0.

title: Renon — occlusion map (visibility per scan position)
description: Occlusion/visibility analysis (CANOPy concept, GeoSense Freiburg) on the synthetic HELIOS++ scan of the Renon inventory, 6 TLS positions. Coloured by the number of positions from which a point received returns: RED = seen from only ONE position (one-sided, prone to occlusion), GREEN = freely visible from several. This shows where a single-scan inventory is blind — the geometric core of the 'single-scan occlusion' limitation. On the synthetic scan it is the clean test case (positions and truth known). CANOPy itself is not (yet) public; the concept is implemented here in the spirit of the suite (scripts/occlusion_map.py).

title: Renon — synthetic TLS scan (HELIOS++)
description: Terrestrial laser scan SIMULATED with HELIOS++ from the single-tree inventory (87 trees) of the same Renon site: procedural tree models (stem + crown, from DBH/height) at their measured positions, sampled from several TLS positions. 2,329,411 points (after thinning), coloured by height. The value lies in the KNOWN truth — every tree parameter is set, not estimated: a basis for benchmarking inventory algorithms and for scenarios (rescanning stands projected with TreeGrOSS). Not a real measurement. Simulator: HELIOS++ (3DGeo Heidelberg); scene from scripts/helios_scene.py.

title: Renon — 3D Gaussian splatting (walkable)
description: Photorealistic 3D Gaussian splatting model of the Renon site, trained from 20 pinhole images (4 positions) with LiDAR initialisation — 700,000 Gaussians. Freely walkable (WASD/mouse) instead of jumping between positions: free movement with correct parallax is the added value over panoramas. Note: the 4 positions lie almost on a line (~10 m) — along it the model looks sharp, across it parallax is missing (streaks). A denser capture would resolve this. Dataset from E57 (build_colmap.py), trained with graphdeco 3DGS on an RTX A4500.

title: Hedge network, Netherlands — Hedge Vertical Index (ALS)
description: Open ALS point cloud (AHN, ~21 pts/m²) of a 1 × 1 km field section. 173 hedge segments, coloured by the Hedge Vertical Index (HVI 0.20–0.80): a composite structural index of vertical complexity (FHD, VCI, number and evenness of layers, weight 0.50), volume/size (0.15) and heterogeneity (0.25). Ground and surroundings stay muted as a backdrop. Markers carry all metrics per segment. Hedge polygons are derived from the canopy height model (height 1–8 m, small linear objects), NOT mapped — segment boundaries and the separation from tree rows are correspondingly fuzzy. The HVI is also RELATIVE: hvi_rescale normalises to the 2nd–98th percentile of THIS section; a value of 0.8 means 'structurally rich compared with the other hedges here', not absolute. Species response curves are uncalibrated starting values. One metric adds nothing here: cover_frac is exactly 1.00 in all 173 segments because the segments are derived FROM the vegetation mask, where cover is necessarily complete — the volume/size sub-index thus effectively shrinks to height. With mapped hedge polygons (e.g. UKCEH for England) cover_frac would measure gaps in the hedge line and carry information again. Above the 3D view the colouring can be switched: by HVI structure or by habitat suitability for five target species (red-backed shrike, common whitethroat, yellowhammer, bat commuting route, wild-bee margin) — suitability is a weighted fuzzy mean of response curves per metric (shrub_div); the curves are uncalibrated starting values. Source: AHN, CC BY 4.0; index: shrub_div/HVI.

title: Renon / ICOS IT-Ren — setup 01
description: Uneven-aged ~200-year-old Norway spruce stand, Renon (South Tyrol), 1735 m. Markers carry vitality attributes derived from RGB (module 4, coloured relative to the stand) and a walkable growth projection to 2044 (module 5, TreeGrOSS demonstrator).
